chapter_theme: The line of gurus (குரு பாரம்பரியம்): Tirumular names the masters who received Nandi's grace, himself among eight, and the seven disciples who carry his mantra on; everything he has, he says, came by Nandi's grace, and the Lord charged the four Nandis with keeping the observances.
structure_note: The eight who received Nandi's grace (67), Tirumular's debt to Nandi (68), his seven disciples (69), and the four Nandis made masters and given their charge (70 to 72).

67.reading: If you seek the masters who received Nandi's grace: the four Nandis, the great sage Sivayoga, Patanjali and Vyaghra who worshipped at the hall, these with me make eight.
67.nuance: மன்று is the hall where Siva dances, by tradition Chidambaram, where Patanjali and Vyaghrapada are said to have seen the dance. The count is four plus three plus Tirumular himself.

68.reading: By Nandi's grace we gained the name of master; by Nandi's grace we sought out Mulan; what can Nandi's grace not do? With Nandi showing the way, I stayed in this land.
68.nuance: மூலனை நாடினோம் is traditionally taken of the body of Mulan the cowherd, which the sage entered and lived in; it may also mean seeking the root (மூலம்). The verse itself does not tell the story.

69.reading: Those who received the mantra in due succession, Malangan, Indran, Soman, Brahman, Rudran, Kalangi with Kanduru before his name, and Kanjamalaiyan, these seven are of my line.
69.nuance: Malangan and Indran are addressed later in the preface (75, 77). To make seven, கந்துரு is taken as a qualifier of காலாங்கி rather than a separate name; it could be read as an eighth name, and its sense is unclear.

70.reading: The four masters, one for each of the four directions, the four who took up many kinds of meaning, the four told 'may you gain all that I gained', the four became gods and became masters.
70.nuance: The four are probably the four Nandis of 67. Who says 'may you gain all that I gained' is not stated: Nandi, the Lord, or Tirumular. The phrase recalls 85, where Tirumular wishes his bliss on the whole world.

71.reading: What the Lord told the three and the four is a greatness beyond death and birth; the god who is the light of the three bright flames did not show that surpassing greatness.
71.nuance: The three and the four are not named. The three flames are traditionally sun, moon and fire. காட்டகிலானே may mean 'could not show' or 'did not show', and so the second half may mean the greatness lies beyond showing. The verse is obscure.

72.reading: 'Even if the flood rises and pours, keep the cool rich observances in all eight directions': so saying, the Lord with cool matted hair like tender coral gave grace to the four who were sunk deep in him.
72.nuance: நியமங்கள் are observances, one of the limbs of yoga in Tirumular's later tantras. எழுந்துநீர் பெய்யினும் may mean 'even if a flood comes' or 'rising, pour water' (an ablution). அழுந்திய (steeped, sunk in) describes the four's devotion.

links.note: Both open 'by Nandi's grace' and both say Tirumular sought Mulan. 68 credits Nandi with his name and his stay in the land; 92 adds what grace did after: he became Sadasiva and entered true wisdom.
